utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this to be a VJ personnel file?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here, "Federal Secretariat for National Defence Personnel Administration," which means that this is a personnel file from the times of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And this is the type of a file that was maintained on people who were members of the VJ, after the JNA became the VJ; do you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I want to look further into this file. If I could have P2424 on the monitor, please. This individual's name is Dane Kosojevic, for the record. It's the file we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to direct your attention to two entries on this page. The first is the penultimate entry where it indicates that the position of the serviceman was the commander of a battalion, and it references the 30th Personnel Centre. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The last entry indicates that the professional military service of this individual was terminated because he was five days absent without leave, and there is in the right-hand side an order number. Do you see that order number, and do you see the acronym PSU?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the number and the acronym, but I don't know what "PSU" stands for. I can only speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. I submit to you, sir, that that is an order of the chief of personnel administration of the Yugoslav Army General Staff. What do you say?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we go to the next exhibit, which is P2425.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document dated the 12th -- I'm sorry, the 8th of December, 1994, and it is from the Drina Corps command, which is a VRS unit. And you will see that it is a proposal for the termination of the professional military service of Ljubo Kosojevic. And who is --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We need to go to the next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell me who has submitted this proposal? Can you see that? Can you read the signature on that, sir? Who committed this proposal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Deputy Commander Colonel Radislav Krstic is what I'm reading here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a -- this is the Drina Corps proposing the termination of Mr. Kosojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we turn to P1807, please. While we're turning to the that Your Honour, the full name of the individual whose personnel file we're looking at is: first name, Ljubo; last name, Kosojevic. His father's name is Dane.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could you repeat the exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, P1807.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, sir, in the last document that we looked at with General Krstic, he was proposing that Mr. Kosojevic be terminated because he had gone AWOL from his unit. This is a document that is issued by the chief of the personnel administration of the Yugoslav Army General Staff dated the 9th of May. We can see the order number on the top, 200/59 corresponds with the number that we saw earlier entered into his personnel file. We can see that the reason that he is being terminated is because he was absent from the service without leave for five consecutive days, specifically what General Krstic had recommended and what he had reported. So, sir, the VJ in fact did discipline and did exercise its authority over VJ personnel for breaches of discipline committed in the VRS; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what arises from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- sir, let me turn to one other portion of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We need to go into private session on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: I think that, given the time, we should adjourn now until 12.30. The Court adjourns. And then you, Mr. Lukic, proceed to your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, I have only a few questions for you. Mr. Harmon asked you yesterday, when he showed you certain documents in order to impeach your testimony provided in the examination-in-chief, and that was that, according to you, the ammunition supplies before 1993 were enough for the VRS, and that from 1993 onwards those supplies dwindled. This is what you asserted, and this is what Mr. Harmon tried to contest. And he showed you some documents: one of them sent to the government -- the Ministry of Defence by General Mladic, and another one drafted by General Milovanovic. According to you, did the Main Staff have enough information about the supplies of units at a lower level? And you told us quite a lot about those supplies, how they were created, and how they were kept a secret. Were they kept a secret from the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was what I stated, and I adhere by my words. Those reserves were being kept a secret from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to read to you part of your answers in the interview with the OTP in 2007 on page 37. My learned friend Mr. Guy-Smith is going to read, because the statement is in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, this will be starting at line 27: "I can claim that the reserve was weakened, but through my channels I received information that units on -- at lower levels, at the levels of brigade, had been hiding their resources and giving false images of resources to Mladic, because I had reliable information and knowledge at the time that those commanders were hiding infantry and artillery ammunition and mines to be able to self-willingly, with co-operation with the local levels of authority, besides the central authority, use the ammunition, meaning to have fund of it."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the last sentence has still not been interpreted into the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, now, General, you stated this for The Hague Tribunal in 2007. Do you still adhere by those words?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I adhere by those words, and this is what I have always claimed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say here that you received the information that you shared --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, when you said that this portion was on page 37, is that 37 of the B/C/S or 37 of the English?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only version I have is the English version. I've never received a B/C/S version. 37 out of 116 at line 27 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, now, could you please clarify one thing for me. You say and you mention your channels through which you received the information that you shared with the OTP; what channels were those, what were the sources of your information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chiefs of the Ministry of Defence departments and municipalities were my subordinates, and they were duty-bound pursuant to the law to replenish units with personnel and materiel and equipment as per the lists. All the units of the VRS which were in the territory of the municipality fell under that obligation. I tasked them with inspect the reserves of ammunition and other equipment. I sometimes personally inspected the depots with them to establish what the situation was. And that was one of my predominant sources of information at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And lets just clarify one more thing with regard to the answers provided to Mr. Harmon. Mr. Harmon asked you about 1993 about the ammunition that was critical at the time. Your answer was a little confusing because it concerned the most important ammunition for the activities of the VRS. Could you please repeat your answer. According to you, what types of ammunition were the most important for the activities of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall repeat, then. And I will supplement my previous answer. Most of the weaponry was infantry weaponry; therefore, the highest quantity of ammunition was required for that type of weaponry. And that was automatic 7.62 Kalashnikov semi-automatic 7.62, machine-gun 7.62 M-84 manufactured by the Crvena Zastava factory in Kragujevac, self-propelled mines that were mounted on semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. That was the answer you gave to Mr. Harmon. I am seeking clarification. At the end of 1993, was all that ammunition in short supply in the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, there was enough of all that ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Harmon put several questions to you with regard to a document which was the decision on the establishment of the commission for materiel supply of the armed forces. Let's clarify an error with regard to the date that Mr. Harmon mentioned on page 26, line 10, which concerns the date of the establishment of that commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please bring up on the screen an OTP document from the 65 ter list, 578.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a decision on the establishment of the state committee for procurement of the armed forces of Republika Srpska. And here we can see a list of names that I'm not going to mention. And it says here that you were appointed the secretary of the committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to page 2 in order to see when the committee was actually established.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The date is 28 March, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this jog your memory? Does it help you remember that the committee was indeed established on that date?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Earlier than I was told by Mr. Harmon, earlier than July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And just one more question with regard to this: The armed forces of Republika Srpska, what did they consist of?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VRS and the Republika Srpska police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document be admitted, Your Honours. We had discussed the work of this committee at great length, and I believe that the document will be of some assistance to the Trial Chamber when it comes to the establishment of facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Let's admit the document and give it an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document should be assigned Exhibit D421. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to go back to another document shown to you by Mr. Harmon. Could the Court please produce P2726. Can we go straight to page 2. I am interested in the portion that you discussed with Mr. Harmon. This is what I would like to shed some more light on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon showed you the lower portion of this document where it says that Mr. Sinisa Borovic drafted this document, where it says: We hereby send you the document. And it says here: Give to Ratko to deal with this. Did you ever hear of Ratko Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the name does ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what his position was and where he was stationed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the logistics staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I no longer need in document, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon showed you another document, P1205.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce the document again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon had a couple of questions about this document. Could you please look at the first page. Could you please read the somewhat lengthy text on page 1 before we move on to page 2. My question is this: On the first page, is there a reference to materiel and equipment or ammunition?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not encountered the word ammunition or any other type of lethal weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go to the second page of the same document. Line 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll read it for you: "I suggest that fuel (400 litres of D-2 and 200 litres of MB-86) be bought in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in the Golubac area and be stored at the Batajnica airfield." Is there any reference to ammunition here or indeed the VJ in that same context?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No reference to ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours, this concludes my re-examination. There is one thing that General Kovacevic would like to say though.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if I may. It's not about this; it's about something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I have some questions based on what Mr. Lukic asked, if I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Because -- let me -- there seems to be a confusion in the record. The witness, in respect of the date of the 20th of June, 1995, that Mr. Lukic refers to, the witness in his evidence testified about being part of a -- I'm looking at page 25. He talks about being part of a group that was formed to deal with the transportation of ammunition across existing borders, and he gave a long explanation about his work in that group, including giving a report to President Karadzic. And then he was asked the question by me as to the commission that you talked about was a commission that was formed on the 20th of June, 1995. My question, Your Honour, was perhaps poorly phrased. The committee for the procurement of arms, the state committee, was indeed formed on the 28th of March, 1995. The group that this witness was a member of, which was the executive team which is part of that committee, was formed on the 20th of June, 1995. So what I'm seeking to do is to clarify the record so there is no confusion whatsoever. That's the only question I have. I want to make sure that when there's a reference to a date and this witness's evidence about an executive team that was formed for the transportation of goods across the border, that the correct date is referred to in the record and there be no confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think it's in keeping with the procedure for Mr. Harmon to be asking questions such as these after my re-examination, but I think this is not in dispute. It was the way Mr. Harmon phrased it, for the committee as we have seen was set up on the 28th of March, 1995, and the witness talked about the activities of his team in June 1995. I wasn't going to ask that question because the question that had been asked previously was about the committee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: I believe the matter has already been clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I do have a small clarification regarding the transcript. My last question, Your Honours - it's something that stems from the document - my question at page 58, line 17. I was reading from the document, Your Honour. It may be a translation issue, but just to make sure. I'm reading that sentence again: "I suggest that fuel and the type of fuel be bought in the FRY." Thank you, Your Honours. Mr. Kovacevic, thank you. Mr. Kovacevic wishes to address the Court. I'm not sure what that is about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I be allowed two minutes to address you, please? I would like to explain the problem in relation to aluminium and my credibility before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, I believe that your testimony already had finished before this Court in the sense that what the procedure allows for you has taken already place. And any other clarification and any other question has been already precluded. So perhaps what you have said is very important now, but yet it's what you have said at the precise procedural opportunity. And having saying so, let me, since you have finished your testimony, thank you very much for appearing in this court. And your task has finished. And we wish you a safe trip back. So please, Court aids, help Mr. Kovacevic to leave the court premises. Thank you very much again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Going back to our next session, is the Defence ready to present the witnesses for our next session that will take place Monday the 19th at 9.00 a.m. in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you very much then. In that case, I wish to thank both the Prosecution and Defence for the procedural promptness which they have shown today and that made possible for us to finish the examination of this witness. And in doing so, we adjourn until Monday the 19th. And thank you again. The Court adjourns.
